strings.name: Anne L’Huillier
strings.summary: Born in Paris, L’Huillier completed doctoral training in France and studied intense laser–atom interactions. She helped discover high-harmonic generation and explain its mechanisms, laying foundations for attosecond light pulses. After moving to Sweden, she pursued experimental and theoretical work at Lund on ultrafast electron dynamics. She shared the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics with Agostini and Krausz, recognizing work built on sustained contributions from multiple research teams.

strings.influence.rationale: Advanced attosecond light-pulse research, providing important experimental methods for observing electron motion and ultrafast physical processes.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Doctoral research at Université Pierre et Marie Curie and the French atomic energy agency (1986).
strings.highlights.h1.title: High-harmonic research
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped observe and explain high harmonics from intense lasers in gases, extending extreme-ultraviolet light sources.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Foundations of attosecond measurement
strings.highlights.h2.text: Developed ultrashort-pulse methods for studying electron dynamics in matter.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Sharing the Nobel Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t1.text: Shared the experimental-methods award with Pierre Agostini and Ferenc Krausz.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sharing the Wolf Prize in Physics
strings.timeline.t2.text: Recognized with Paul Corkum and Krausz for ultrafast lasers and attosecond physics.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Royal Swedish Academy membership
strings.timeline.t3.text: Elected to the academy in recognition of her optics research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Shorter attosecond pulses
strings.timeline.t4.text: The Lund team produced approximately 170-attosecond pulses, advancing time-resolved experiments.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Lund professorship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Established sustained research and teaching in Sweden, developing an attosecond physics group.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining Lund University
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became associate professor, bringing high-harmonic research to Swedish experimental facilities.
strings.timeline.t7.title: High-harmonic discovery
strings.timeline.t7.text: The team observed numerous harmonics from intense laser–gas interactions, opening a route to attosecond pulses.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completing doctoral research
strings.timeline.t8.text: Studied multiphoton and multielectron ionization at Paris VI and the French atomic energy agency.
